26:
And what our Rabbi wrote:
“And if it is in a herd with other animals and its milk got mixed with others, all the cheeses are prohibited” — as it is written afterward.
And the Rashba wrote that we follow the measure of sixty, etc. This implies that according to the first opinion, even more than sixty is also prohibited.
I do not understand why there is a stricter concern with this milk compared to other prohibitions. It is possible that the initial statement was not a separate opinion but rather the beginning of the discussion to say that this milk prohibits its mixture, and he intended to conclude that it only prohibits up to sixty.
However, since the Rashba wrote this explicitly, it was included in his name. Even though, according to this, it would be proper to write “And the Rashba wrote,” and not just “the Rashba wrote,” which implies disagreement, our Rabbi is not particular about this detail, as he often writes “the Rashba” even if he does not disagree.
